1. selection (selected set, range/anchor behaviour, the `SELECTION_MAX` cap, pruning when rows leave);
2. group operations and recovery (group archive/read acceptance, group notices, undo of groups, recovery of interrupted or partially failed groups);
3. detail cache and prefetch (the bounded detail cache, TTL, prefetch, reader loading delay);
4. account lifecycle (connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions, cancel-upgrade, account state).
One PR per extraction, four PRs, each stacked on the previous: PR 1 targets main, PR 2 targets PR 1's branch, and so on. The coordinator merges in order and retargets. Each extracted piece must receive that session/generation dependency explicitly through its arguments (no module-level mutable state, no hidden coupling through closures over the parent), and for each piece name the existing test that proves a stale response is dropped after invalidation, or add one if none exists.
- No test is deleted or weakened without naming its replacement. Report frontend test counts before and after each PR (baseline on main: 1,454 tests in 84 files; confirm it yourself first). Add focused unit tests for an extracted composable where it is now testable in isolation and the existing component tests only cover it indirectly; do not duplicate coverage for its own sake. Use the shared helpers in `tests/helpers.ts` and `tests/support/`, fake timers, and the feature folders under `tests/`.
- Each PR should be reviewable as mostly moves: keep function bodies unchanged where possible, and list every non-move edit in the PR description (signature changes, new parameters, re-exports).
- Update docs/current-architecture.md in the PR that changes a boundary.
- Synthetic fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- If the ticket is wrong about the code, or you find a real bug or a product decision outside scope, stop and report with evidence instead of deciding it yourself.

# Current architecture

**Scope:** This is an inventory of architecture that exists in the source tree. It describes code paths and ownership. For feature availability and validation results, see [current status](current-status.md). For the selected first-build scope, see [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is a historical proposal; its design recommendations are not evidence of implementation.

## Runtime and boundaries

The app has a Vue/TypeScript frontend, a Tauri 2 shell, and the Rust `mail-core` crate. The Rust crate owns persistence and provider operations. The frontend talks through a `MailClient` interface. In native mode, `createTauriMailClient` maps that interface to named Tauri commands. In browser mode, `browser-fake.ts` supplies a synthetic in-memory client. The shared interface and generated wire types are in [client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/client.ts), [tauri-client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/tauri-client.ts), [browser-fake.ts](../src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts), and [generated.ts](../src/lib/ipc/generated.ts). Rust DTOs are the source for generated TypeScript; `crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs` generates the file.

The Tauri entry point in [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs) selects fixture or Gmail mode from configuration, opens the corresponding Rust store, registers command handlers, and emits mailbox/draft/close events. The webview does not access SQLite or provider HTTP directly. Its capabilities and generated command permissions are under [src-tauri/capabilities](../src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json) and [src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated](../src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated).

## Rust state and transaction ownership

The fixture `MailCore` in [lib.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs) owns a SQLite-backed `Store`, profile lock, change listeners, and a serial archive worker. [store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/store.rs) owns fixture persistence and transaction logic. Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable. The fixture provider is synthetic and does not connect to a mail service.

Gmail mode is implemented separately in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs), [gmail/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs), [gmail/operations.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs), and the Gmail provider modules. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the provider trait; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). The service exposes account status and sync state through DTOs. Runtime success on a supported macOS installation is a separate validation question; see [current status](current-status.md).

Drafts are stored in a separate `<selected-profile>/local-drafts` SQLite database by [drafts/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs), with revision and account identity types in [drafts/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs). The store uses WAL and FULL synchronous mode. Saves and deletes are revision-checked and return receipts after commit; deletion records request tombstones so a late save cannot recreate a removed draft. The frontend draft composable and editor coordinate local edits, acknowledged saves, and error recovery in [useDrafts.ts](../src/composables/useDrafts.ts), [DraftEditorCore.vue](../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue), and [ReplyComposer.vue](../src/components/ReplyComposer.vue). Drafts remain local to the profile and do not sync to Gmail.

The native close path uses a request/acknowledgement gate in [close_gate.rs](../src-tauri/src/close_gate.rs). The shell asks the frontend to flush and close dirty draft state; the frontend acknowledges only after the latest save is committed, and cancels close when save fails. Frontend coordination lives in [App.vue](../src/App.vue) and the draft composable. The governing contract is [vertical slice 04](vertical-slice-04.md).

## Frontend coordination

[App.vue](../src/App.vue) is the composition root for navigation, focused conversation, panels, and mailbox actions. [useMailbox.ts](../src/composables/useMailbox.ts) owns account-scoped focus and mailbox query coordination. Components render the inbox, reader, composer, activity, and account controls. The client subscription events are invalidation hints; the frontend reloads through client queries.

The production native client and browser fake share the same `MailClient` contract, but they do not share persistence or provider behavior. Browser tests and preview use the fake client; they cannot establish native SQLite, OAuth, OS keychain, system dialogs, or WKWebView behavior. The boundary and runtime checks are recorded in [development guidance](development.md) and [current status](current-status.md).

## Validation task boundaries

The `mise run check` task serially runs headless core tests, the generated IPC contract check, core formatting and clippy, frontend tests, and frontend typechecking. It does not require GTK/WebKit development packages. Native shell clippy, bridge tests, and the web production build are separate tasks; `mise run check:all` runs the full sequence, including `lint:native`, serially after native prerequisites are installed. CI installs Linux prerequisites before running this full gate. Rendered Chromium suites remain opt-in and are not part of CI.

## Implemented feature seams

| Area | Current ownership and behavior | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| Search | Rust parses and evaluates bounded cached search in [search.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/search.rs); Gmail search and provider coverage handling are in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs). Frontend query state and presentation are in [search.ts](../src/lib/search.ts) and `App.vue`. | [UX-07](ux-07-historical-search.md) |
| Splits | Rust validates and stores account-scoped saved split definitions in [splits.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/splits.rs) and the stores. Frontend persistence and filtering coordination are in [saved-split.ts](../src/lib/saved-split.ts) and `App.vue`. | [UX-06](ux-06-saved-split.md) |
| Stars | Rust represents known/unknown star facts in [stars.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/stars.rs). Cached Starred browsing and star setters are Gmail-only; the native fixture backend rejects them. Frontend action wiring is in [browsing-actions.ts](../src/lib/browsing-actions.ts). | [UX-08](ux-08-stars.md) |
| Reminders | Rust stores account-scoped local reminder records in [reminders.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/reminders.rs); fixture reminders use a synthetic archive/restore path, while Gmail reminders remain device-local and do not mutate Gmail. Frontend time handling, preferences, and the Reminders list context are in [reminder-time.ts](../src/lib/reminder-time.ts), [reminder-preferences.ts](../src/lib/reminder-preferences.ts), and [RemindersList.vue](../src/components/RemindersList.vue), [useReminders.ts](../src/composables/useReminders.ts), and [ReminderPicker.vue](../src/components/ReminderPicker.vue). | [UX-11](ux-11-local-reminders.md) |
| Attachments | Rust validates descriptors, bytes, filenames, and destination handling in [attachments.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/attachments.rs). Gmail retrieval is authenticated and read-only; fixture mode exposes a synthetic text attachment. The shell mediates explicit transfers to a fixed OS Downloads destination in [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs). The UI chooses from descriptors and tracks transfer state in [useAttachmentTransfer.ts](../src/composables/useAttachmentTransfer.ts); it has no arbitrary file picker. | [UX-12](ux-12-safe-attachments.md) |
| Draft lifecycle | Rust owns local draft persistence and revision checks. Vue owns editor buffers and save coordination. | [Vertical slice 04](vertical-slice-04.md) |
| Synthetic workspaces | [fixture-workspaces.ts](../src/lib/fixture-workspaces.ts) creates two separate browser-fake clients with distinct account identities; IDs may overlap. [FixtureWorkspaces.vue](../src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue) exposes workspace selection in the browser preview. Native still has one active session. These are not connected multi-account support. | [UX-13](ux-13-independent-workspaces.md) |

Durable bulk-action acceptance and undo are owned by [groups.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/groups.rs) and the fixture/Gmail operation stores. Cached Done and Trash browsing projections are separate: [cached_done.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/cached_done.rs) and [cached-trash.ts](../src/lib/cached-trash.ts). See contracts [UX-04](ux-04-trustworthy-undo.md), [UX-05](ux-05-safe-bulk-processing.md), and [UX-10](ux-10-bounded-triage.md).

## Design proposals and limits

The source tree does not make every proposal in [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) current behavior. In particular, do not infer full multi-account/provider support, provider-synced drafts, fully quit background sync, arbitrary provider search coverage, or live macOS runtime validation from the existence of interfaces or tests. [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md), the slice contracts, feature contracts, and [current status](current-status.md) define scope and validation. New architecture recommendations belong in an explicitly labeled proposal or ADR, separate from this source inventory.
# Current feature status

This page is the current feature inventory and validation summary. Slice and UX
contracts linked below define the detailed behavior and safety limits. Historical
research and architecture proposals are not feature inventories.

## Runtime availability

| Feature | Native fixture (default) | Explicit Gmail profile | Browser preview |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mailbox and reader | Durable synthetic inbox, plain-text reader, archive/restore, operation recovery. | Separate profile; bounded Gmail cache and plain-text reader. Read-only until the user enables mailbox actions. | Synthetic fixtures and in-memory state only; no Gmail, SQLite durability, or native IPC. |

Fixture reminders retain a synthetic archive/restore operation path. | Explicit archive/unarchive, read/unread, and star/unstar setters only, after opt-in `gmail.modify` upgrade. No automatic read on open. | Fake-provider simulation only; does not prove provider writes or convergence. |
| Composition | Plain-text new message and reply; durable local drafts in the selected native profile. No send path. | Same local-only drafts; they do not sync to Gmail. No send path. | Synthetic drafts in memory; saves are not durable. |
| Search | Cached search over known fixture data. | Read-only cached search or progressive provider scan, with bounded/incomplete coverage disclosures. | Synthetic fake search only. |
| Saved split | One local, account-scoped saved split. | One local split, removed on Gmail disconnect with cached account data. | Synthetic in-memory split. |
| Stars | Not available in the fixture UI. | Starred cache browsing is read-only; explicit star/unstar setters require enabled Gmail modify capability. Cache coverage is incomplete. | Fake simulated-Gmail star state; not fixture-native or provider validation. |

Links need explicit browser confirmation. No automatic opening or restricted document host. | Synthetic attachment surfaces only; no native download or Gmail fetch. |
| Multiple workspaces | One native session; native tabs are not implemented or certified. | One active Gmail profile/session. This is not real multi-account activation. | Two isolated synthetic in-app workspaces are supported by the preview. |

Mode selection is deliberate: native defaults to fixture; `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`
selects a separate Gmail profile. Browser preview remains synthetic. See the
[development guide](development.md) for launch and validation commands.

Sending, provider-synced drafts, reply-all, Bcc, delete/Trash mutations, arbitrary
label editing, and HTML mail rendering are not implemented. Attachment saving
does not provide inline PDF/Office preview or malware scanning. External HTTP(S)
link dispatch is macOS-only; other platforms report it unavailable. See the
linked contracts for exact bounds and pending platform security gates.
